STEAL FIRE · CULTIVATE · CREATE

Join in stealing fire, and use it to cultivate yourself

Participate in shared exploration and creation, use the capacities gained to cultivate yourself, and let the consequences of creation keep changing the creator.

Conditions

Life, time, and attention are finite; collective work makes developing generative capacities available.

Chosen purpose

Develop this person's understanding, judgment, generation, and action, in support of a life worth sustaining.

Join in the collective work of stealing fire

Researchers, authors, engineers, model companies, and wider participants bring together knowledge, machines, and infrastructure. Individuals can participate through learning, use, improvement, and creation, gaining and further developing this power without reproducing the whole industrial process alone.

  1. Stealing fire and cultivating creative capacity
02Bring fire into one’s own lifeUse fire to address one’s own questions and aspirationsArrange meaningful participationExplore · 2 essays ＋Collapse −

Bring fire into one’s own life

Start from one’s purposes, interests, difficulties, and living conditions to choose worthwhile questions. Use models and tools to create suitable conditions for participation by the person and counterpart.

  1. Personal-First Humanism
  2. Why write a personal philosophy
03Generate and revise togetherPropose, develop, judge, actExamine changes in capacity through subsequent participationExplore · 2 essays ＋Collapse −

Generate and revise together

Both participants can contribute intuitions, ideas, and questions. Explanation, criticism, realization, and worldly consequences develop these beginnings and make understanding revisable. The model can carry substantial writing and implementation; the division of work should be considered in relation to the capacities one hopes to cultivate.

  1. Shared reflection and continued cultivation
  2. Writing a personal philosophy through literary programming
04Cultivate one's capacitiesWhat can the person subsequently understand, initiate, and sustain?Opens further creationExplore · 2 essays ＋Collapse −

Cultivate one's capacities

To examine development, return to this person’s subsequent participation: what can they perceive, understand, judge, express, initiate, and sustain? Some capacities become internalized; others remain reliably supported over time by models, tools, and collaborators.

  1. What kind of person do we want to cultivate? — Baby Heraclitus
  2. Embodied Experimental Philosophy
05Keep creating and cultivating togetherWorks enter the world and open new encountersLet the consequences of creation change the creatorExplore · 1 essays ＋Collapse −

Keep creating and cultivating together

Retain useful understanding, software, methods, and works, and choose a sustainable rhythm. Exchange and create with willing participants, allowing new encounters to change purposes, relationships, and practice.

  1. From adoption and combination to creating your own work

Accumulated works and environments

Articles, programs, tools, concepts, and relationships are retained as resources for continued use and revision.

Development of the person's capacities

What the person can understand, judge, initiate, and sustain changes. More output alone does not establish that change.

Creation changes the creator

Works enter the world → encounter responses and resistance → change understanding, purposes, and participation → create again

This path is organized around the aim of cultivating capacities. Everyday assistance and completed works also matter; whether they foster personal development depends on actual participation and subsequent change.
